toolNote: `tool` names the client tool that places this machine, so a new machine appears in the tool column as soon as it exists here.
note: Machines, as opposed to matter. Entities are a separate layer from the particle grid (spec 4.1) — a cell holds sand or water, never a machine. Adding an entity should be an edit here plus one behaviour arm in crates/sim-core/src/entities.rs, and nothing else.
goldNote: `goldPer` is how many points of product a press must take in to make one cell of currency. It is a machine property rather than a global, so a better press mints more from the same input. A press takes only what it can press; everything else falls through, which is why it never competes with the reaction feeding it. Nuggets appear in place and fall out of the machine — storage is a vault (spec 5.1).
mouthNote: `mouthOffset`/`mouthWidth` are where an emitter's opening actually is, in cells from the tile's left edge. Sim-core cannot read the sprite pixels below (spec 8.3 keeps it rendering-free), so these are authored by hand to match whatever the running sprite's funnel narrows to. Absent means the whole tile width, which is correct for anything that is not an emitter.
spriteNote: Sprites are 9x9 char grids, one tile (spec 2.3). `when.row` picks art for one row of a footprint taller than a tile, counting from the top, so a two-tile machine can have a head and a body instead of one tile stamped twice; absent matches every row. '#' shell, '=' shadowed shell, ''' trim, 'o' the opening, which takes the colour of whatever the entity is working on. Space is transparent and lets the world show through. The first rule whose `when` matches is used, so order them most specific first. `elementState` matches the state of the element the entity handles, which means a new element of an existing state gets a shape without anyone drawing one. `pixels` can be one 9-row grid, or an array of them for animation — sim-wasm cycles frames by tick, no client change needed.
beltNote: Belt and filter are both behaviour `belt` (spec 4.1-4.3): the same machine, distinguished only by whether an instance names an element to let through, exactly like one `emitter` tool is tuned per instance by which element it emits. `chassis` names the indestructible element `World.place` fills the tile's own footprint with, so gravity holds cargo up on it the same way it holds anything up on solid ground.
paceNote: `rate` is how much a machine does per action; `interval` is how many ticks it waits between actions (1 = every tick, the default). Both are here rather than in code because pacing is tuning, and tuning wants to be a data edit. Playtesting found everything roughly six times too fast: the host also halved the tick rate, and these intervals take the rest out. A belt at interval 3 moves about a tile a second, which is the reference point everything else was set against.
heaterNote: Burns `input` (fuel) to hold its own footprint at `heatOutput` Kelvin while fed (spec 5.3) — no banking, the same shape a compactor has none. The generic conduction pass in crates/sim-core/src/heat.rs carries that into whatever touches it, and cools the footprint back down on its own once fuel runs out; nothing here needs a cooldown.

sprites.note: Nothing to press. A press with nothing in it is not broken, it is unfed — usually a routing mistake worth seeing.

entities.note: A place, not a machine. The player digs a pit, walls it, and declares the inside a vault; gold that lands in one is money. Its footprint is whatever was marked out, so widthTiles and heightTiles here are only the default for a single click.
entities.name: vault

entities.note: Conveys whatever rests on top of it (spec 4.1-4.2). Its own footprint is filled with `structure` the moment it is placed, so gravity holds cargo up on it like any other floor. Two frames on the tread row are the whole animation: enough to read as motion.
entities.name: belt

sprites.note: Jammed: cargo is on it but cannot advance.

entities.note: A belt that lets one element fall through its underside instead of conveying it (spec 4.3) — the same behaviour as `belt`, tuned per instance by `element`, the way one `emitter` tool is tuned by which element it emits. The opening takes that element's colour, same as an emitter's mouth.
entities.name: filter

sprites.note: Jammed, same as a plain belt — the opening only appears once it is actually passing its element through.

entities.note: Burns fuel to hold its own footprint hot (spec 5.3) — the machine that finally gives fuel a consumer. Radiates via the generic conduction pass, not a special case; it carries no element, the same as a press.
entities.name: heater

entities.note: A belt that conducts (spec 4.1-4.2). Mechanically it is `belt` with one field changed — `chassis` names kilnStructure instead of beltStructure — and that is deliberate: `convey` and `convey_one` are untouched, so a kiln carries cargo exactly the way a belt does. What differs is thermal. Cargo rides the row directly above the body, so on a kiln it is in contact with a 2.0-conductivity floor rather than a 0.0 one, and a heater set against the run heats everything the run is carrying. Length is therefore residence time and heaters are temperature, both of them things the player draws rather than sets. Nothing stops moving to be heated, which is the point: a pile that has to sit somewhere hot is a jam waiting to happen.
entities.name: kiln

sprites.note: Jammed, same as a plain belt: the tread stops.
The belt silhouette, so it reads as one, with a barred interior instead of a plain one — the same visual grammar the heater's grate uses, saying this stretch of transport is also an element.

entities.note: Carries matter upward, which nothing else does (spec 11 question 1): gravity goes down, belts go sideways, and neither ever decreases a cell's y. Without it the refine chain cannot close — fuel compacts at the bottom of a silo and the heaters that burn it sit above. A shaft, not a machine that swallows and re-emits: each beat the column inside its footprint shifts up one cell and the top cell steps out, so what comes out is the particles that went in (spec 4.2). It does not fight gravity and does not need to — the column rests on whatever is under the shaft, the way a belt's cargo rests on the belt. Feed one by running a belt directly beneath: a belt's carry row IS the bottom row of a lift standing on it, so they compose with no special case. Height is the player's, like a vault's footprint, and a taller shaft costs longer to prime before anything comes out the top. `interval` is 4 against a belt's 3, so going up is deliberately dearer than going along.
entities.name: lift

sprites.note: Backed up: something is at the mouth with nowhere to step out to.
Two frames of a chain climbing the shaft. The casing holds still; only the rungs move, so it reads as lifting rather than as the whole tower sliding.
